facts.text: Shahayuh of the South Road paid for the Great Bridge from his own pocket; his name is cut into every stone, which the old blood finds vulgar.
Old-blood lords keep 'accidentally' damaging the Great Bridge, and Shahayuh of the South Road suspects his fellow Banner Lord.
Haʻahoqo the General has quietly begun counting how many soldiers would follow him, rather than the Throne, if the emperor died.
Paqax Chain-breaker had the shackles he wore as a slave set into the Block.
Waarua of the Harbour no longer has keys to all of the council hall's locked ledger rooms.
Kitim Duel-ender once killed in a duel, and started the Dueling Society so no one else would have to.
A double sits in for Gahìru of the Great House at public audiences when his hands shake.
The Binders have offered Nemu of the Wide Bay a price for the list of runaways sheltered at the Anchorage.
Kotqot Wall-breaker took Breakwall by smashing a hole through its outer wall, and left it open: whoever can hold the breach can have the keep.
Kotqot Wall-breaker keeps a written record of every lie the Throne has told, to publish the day he declares independence.
Kotqot Wall-breaker defies the Throne because he thinks it a lie, not out of greed.
Hotorìṭo the High Priest no longer believes, and has stopped performing the inner rites; no one has checked in years.
Gure of the Herb-Stream House guards the way to the Womb of Creation, whose location is never spoken.
Yaweth of the Market Road is planning the biggest score in the island's history.
Ḍolo of the Four-Ring House has kept a copy of every favor done for the old houses, and they've stopped answering his letters.
The Road Crews are close to voting to strike against Sharp Hands rates; one bought vote would decide it.
Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House rules the Ninth Ring's archive from memory; it has gaps only he knows about.
Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House has begun to forget.
Tuhuḍo of the Ninth-Ring House knows the Alliance is dying, and is worn out from holding it up.

The Sharp Hands' three partners, Feyesh of the Silver Road, Dorog Coin-counter and Kodor Debt-taker, quietly profit from the Binder trade; a cellar below the Counting-House keeps the second set of books.
The Mount wants the Low Shrine closed, and Qeḍuʻata of the Rain-Shore House has more followers than she realizes.
Doruḍoqu the Carter has called the Road Crews to vote in the Long Shed on striking against the Counting-House's rates.
Kodor Debt-taker has let it be known that any crew that strikes will have its notes called in.
Young warriors at the Proving Ground call for a raid below the Rim; Totkit Sea-crosser has forbidden it until the Height's stores are counted.
Textrim, High Priestess, has sent word below the Rim that the Height will hear any offer of grain made with respect.
Hotorìṭo the High Priest has ordered the Low Shrine's soup kitchen at Elderhollow closed; Qeḍuʻata of the Rain-Shore House keeps it open every evening.
Pilgrims who stopped climbing to the Mount now leave their coin at the Low Shrine, and the Mount's preachers call Qeḍuʻata of the Rain-Shore House's way a heresy.
Litiṭaʻa of the Great House knows how weak the emperor has grown, and hides it behind the court's ceremony.
Momilei of the Deep Reef knows that boats slip out from Reefhold to the Far Sails at night, and allows it.
Garoṭaqa of the First-Stone House is digging under the Founding Stone for older records to prove the True Line's claim.
Linuha of the Star Harbour has mapped a path deeper into the green than anyone has gone, and found something that walks there with purpose.
Textrim's Height is one hard winter from hunger; Textrim, High Priestess, would trade peace for grain if anyone offered it with respect.
Young warriors at the Proving Ground want war with the lowlands; Totkit Sea-crosser is holding them back by a thread.
Fiyeweya of No Road is never at the Wayhouse; she judges by letter, read out by the eldest copyist.
